rawFindings.title: Parser Initialization Location Changed Without Reset on Reconnect
rawFindings.explanation: The parser (this.reply_parser) is now initialized in the RedisClient constructor instead of in the create_stream function. Previously, the parser was recreated each time create_stream was called (e.g., on reconnects), effectively resetting the parser's internal state. Now, since create_stream no longer resets the parser, there is a risk that the parser's internal buffer may retain leftover data during reconnects, causing parsing errors or incorrect command replies.
rawFindings.suggestion: Move the parser initialization back into the create_stream function or ensure the parser is reset properly upon reconnect to avoid stale parser states.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Create a client, partially consume some input so the parser has buffer data, then force a reconnect. The parser does not reset its buffer, and subsequent replies may be corrupted or fail to parse correctly.
